$comment: Source manifest for the planned RAG corpus. Planning data only — the app does not read this file yet. See docs/source_strategy.md for the strategy and docs/rag_architecture.md for the architecture. 'ingest' values: planned (license-clean, will be fetched/chunked in a later stage), curated (we author it ourselves), link_only (copyrighted — metadata/URL reference only, never ingested).

sources.title: Summa Theologiae (selected articles)
sources.author: Thomas Aquinas
sources.translator: Fathers of the English Dominican Province
sources.licenseNote: 1920 English Dominican Province translation is public domain in the US. Mirrors: CCEL, sacred-texts, isidore.co. New Advent hosts the same translation.
sources.chunking: One article per chunk (question/objections/sed contra/respondeo/replies). Citation ID: Part, Question, Article (e.g. 'ST I-II, Q.94, a.2'). Selected articles only — Five Ways, natural law, virtue, soul, essence/existence — not the full text.
sources.notes: The most retrieval-friendly primary text in the corpus; each article is a self-contained Q&A unit.

sources.title: De Ente et Essentia (On Being and Essence)
sources.author: Thomas Aquinas
sources.translator: TBD - confirm a public-domain translation before ingesting
sources.licenseNote: Public-domain translations exist; confirm the specific edition's status before fetching.
sources.notes: Essence/existence distinction; supports the metaphysics position cards.

sources.title: Thus Spake Zarathustra
sources.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
sources.chunking: One named section/discourse per chunk. Citation ID: part + discourse title.
sources.notes: Translation is dated vs. Kaufmann (copyrighted). Fine for grounding/citation anchoring; the persona prompt carries voice.

sources.title: Beyond Good and Evil
sources.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
sources.chunking: One numbered aphorism per chunk. Citation ID: 'Beyond Good and Evil §N'.

sources.title: On the Genealogy of Morals
sources.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
sources.chunking: One numbered section per chunk. Citation ID: essay + section (e.g. 'Genealogy II.12').
sources.notes: Core source for ressentiment / slave morality cards.

sources.title: The Joyful Wisdom (The Gay Science)
sources.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
sources.chunking: One numbered aphorism per chunk. Citation ID: 'The Gay Science §N'.
sources.notes: §125 (the madman) and §343 anchor the death-of-God cards.

sources.title: Twilight of the Idols / The Antichrist
sources.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
sources.licenseNote: Both public domain in the US.
sources.notes: Twilight 'Maxims and Arrows' §8 is the verified source of 'what does not kill me...'.

sources.title: Selections from the Writings of Kierkegaard
sources.author: Søren Kierkegaard
sources.licenseNote: Published 1923; public domain in the US (Project Gutenberg #60333). The only substantial PD English Kierkegaard.
sources.chunking: By selection, subdivided at natural breaks; each chunk tagged with the original work it excerpts (e.g. 'Fear and Trembling, via Hollander 1923').
sources.notes: Hong (Princeton) and Swenson/Lowrie (1936+) translations remain copyrighted — do not ingest. Kierkegaard is otherwise card-heavy; cards must record which pseudonym argues what.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (relevant entries)
sources.author: Various
sources.licenseNote: NEVER ingest. Primary authority for writing position cards; record entry + section in each card's provenance.

sources.title: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy (relevant entries)
sources.author: Various
sources.licenseNote: NEVER ingest. Secondary authority for cards.

sources.title: Wikiquote (sourced sections only)
sources.author: Community
sources.licenseNote: Ingestable with attribution. Use SOURCED sections only; record disputed/misattributed quotes explicitly as warnings.
sources.chunking: One quote per entry with exact-location citation; misattribution notes attached.
sources.notes: Directly attacks the fabricated-quotation failure mode.

sources.title: Wikipedia biography articles
sources.author: Community
sources.licenseNote: Ingestable with attribution. Biography/timeline facts only — not interpretive positions.

sources.title: Introduction to Philosophy series (Rebus Community)
sources.author: Various
sources.licenseNote: Genuinely ingestable, but organized by topic rather than philosopher. Low priority.
sources.notes: Revisit for beginner-level topical grounding if needed.

sources.title: Position cards (authored in-house)
sources.author: Project (Claude-assisted, human-verified)
sources.licenseNote: Our own synthesis in our own words; provenance recorded per card. Corpus backbone.
sources.chunking: One position per card; format in docs/source_strategy.md. Target ~30-60 per philosopher.
sources.notes: Sartre and Camus rely almost entirely on cards + works index (no ingestable primary text — all works in copyright; Camus d. 1960, Sartre d. 1980).

sources.title: Works indexes (authored in-house)
sources.author: Project
sources.licenseNote: One small document per philosopher: each major work, date, one sentence on what it argues.
sources.notes: Answers 'where is this argued?' even when chunk-level retrieval misses.
